topic: Discovery of Electrons, Protons and Neutrons
title: What Is Inside an Atom? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A neon sign glows, a comb lifts tiny bits of paper, and a spark jumps from your finger to a door handle. One tiny particle is behind all three. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we find the three particles inside every atom, and see how each one was caught.

On the molecule bench, a discharge tube with almost all the air pumped out sends a ray from the cathode to the anode. It lights a zinc sulphide coating and bends towards the positive plate: a stream of negative particles, the same for every metal and gas. These are electrons. With holes in the cathode, canal rays stream the other way and bend towards the negative plate; the lightest of them, from hydrogen, is the proton. We combine Thomson's e/m (1.758820 × 10^11 C kg^-1) with the charge e (1.602176 × 10^-19 C) to get the electron's mass, 9.109 × 10^-31 kg, watch Chadwick's neutrons (1932) fly through an electric field without bending, and compare all three particles from the NCERT table. A worked example shows Millikan's idea that charge comes in whole packets of e. Then the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 14 of our PUC Chemistry series and the first episode of Chapter 2.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
